cards.name: Industrial Efficiency
cards.flavor: Every wasted joule was a choice.

codex.title: Industrial energy efficiency
codex.body: Waste-heat recovery, electric motors and smarter process control are among the cheapest large-scale mitigation available. IPCC AR6 ranks industrial efficiency as a gigaton-scale lever this decade.

cards.name: Clean Energy Grid
cards.flavor: Sun and wind, wired to the furnaces.

codex.title: Clean electrification
codex.body: Wind and solar are now the cheapest new electricity in most of the world. Electrifying industry on a clean grid removes the largest single block of global emissions (IEA net-zero roadmap).

cards.name: Circular Economy
cards.flavor: Nothing is waste; everything is feedstock.

codex.title: Circular material flows
codex.body: Roughly a quarter of industrial emissions come from making virgin materials. Reuse, remanufacture and recycling cut both emissions and extraction (Project Drawdown).

cards.name: Industrial Symbiosis
cards.flavor: One factory's exhaust is another's furnace.

codex.title: Industrial symbiosis
codex.body: In Kalundborg, Denmark, factories have traded exhaust steam, cooling water and by-products since 1972. One plant's waste stream becomes another's input - profitably.

cards.name: Industrial Carbon Levy
cards.flavor: The polluters pay. The voters notice.

codex.title: Carbon pricing
codex.body: Carbon pricing makes polluters pay per ton and funds the transition; over 70 schemes now cover about a quarter of global emissions. It works - and it is politically explosive when the revenue is not visibly returned to people.

cards.name: Rail & Bike Networks
cards.flavor: The fastest way through a city was never a car.

codex.title: Modal shift
codex.body: Shifting trips to rail and cycling is an IPCC AR6 avoid-shift lever: it cuts emissions, air pollution and health costs at once. Copenhagen's bike lanes pay for themselves in public health alone.

cards.name: Affordable EVs
cards.flavor: Electric, efficient, and priced for everyone.

codex.title: Electric vehicles for all
codex.body: EVs cut lifecycle emissions even on today's grids, and battery costs fell about 90% in a decade. The lever is affordability: EVs only decarbonize transport when ordinary households can buy them.

cards.name: Walkable Cities
cards.flavor: Streets returned to the people who live on them.

codex.title: Compact urbanism
codex.body: The 15-minute-city idea puts daily needs within a walk. Compact, mixed-use neighborhoods cut car-kilometers structurally - an avoided ton is cheaper than any abated one (IPCC AR6 Ch.5).

cards.name: Plant-Rich Diet Campaign
cards.flavor: Good for the land, good for the heart.

codex.title: Plant-rich diets
codex.body: The EAT-Lancet Commission found a mostly plant-based diet could feed 10 billion people within planetary boundaries. Project Drawdown ranks plant-rich diets among the top climate solutions of all.

cards.name: Agroecology Transition
cards.flavor: Farms that feed the soil as well as the people.

codex.title: Agroecology
codex.body: Agroecology builds soil carbon with cover crops, agroforestry and rotation instead of synthetic inputs. Healthy soils are the second-largest carbon store on land after forests.

cards.name: Food Commons
cards.flavor: A meal shared is a system changed.

codex.title: Food waste and food commons
codex.body: Community food programs cut waste - a third of all food is lost - and shift diets by making the sustainable option the default. Food waste reduction is Project Drawdown's top-ranked solution.

cards.name: Reforestation Program
cards.flavor: Plant today what must breathe for a century.

codex.title: Reforestation
codex.body: Restoring forests is the largest proven negative-emissions option available today. It is slow carbon: a planted forest absorbs for decades, which is why starting early matters so much.

cards.name: Peatland & Ocean Repair
cards.flavor: The oldest carbon capture technology on Earth.

codex.title: Peatland and ocean sinks
codex.body: Peatlands hold twice the carbon of all forests on 3% of the land; drained peat burns for years. Rewetting them, and protecting seagrass and kelp, locks the oldest carbon stores shut.

cards.name: Blue Carbon Program
cards.flavor: Mangroves hold the coast and the carbon.

codex.title: Blue carbon
codex.body: Mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass bury carbon up to 40 times faster per hectare than tropical forest - and they blunt storm surges for free while doing it.

cards.name: Adaptive Infrastructure
cards.flavor: Build for the storms we already ordered.

codex.title: Climate-proof infrastructure
codex.body: Adaptation is now unavoidable spending: elevated grids, cool roofs, hardened water systems. Every dollar of resilient infrastructure saves several in avoided disaster losses (World Bank).

cards.name: Independent Media Fund
cards.flavor: A public that understands will demand the change.

codex.title: Independent climate journalism
codex.body: Public understanding of climate tracks the quality of the information environment. Independent journalism measurably raises support for transition policy - and inoculates against denial campaigns.

cards.name: Global Wellbeing Fund
cards.flavor: A transition nobody enjoys is a transition nobody keeps.

codex.title: Wellbeing economics
codex.body: IPCC AR6 Chapter 5's key finding: demand-side change works only when wellbeing rises with it. Universal services - health, transit, energy access - decouple a good life from a high-carbon one.

cards.name: Transition Festivals
cards.flavor: Celebrate what works and it spreads.

codex.title: Social contagion of change
codex.body: Visible collective wins normalize change: car-free days, harvest festivals, retrofit street parties. Behaviors spread through social networks - contagion is a real mitigation channel.

cards.name: Public Support Fund
cards.flavor: Never again govern past the people.

codex.title: Just-transition funds
codex.body: France's 2018 fuel-tax revolt taught the textbook lesson: climate policy that ignores distribution fails politically. Rebates and just-transition funds keep the public inside the coalition.

cards.name: Form Alliance
cards.flavor: We cannot command the world. We can convince it.

codex.title: Climate clubs
codex.body: Coalitions with shared standards and preferential terms let ambitious countries move without waiting for unanimity - the climate-club economics of William Nordhaus.

cards.name: Joint Transition Project
cards.flavor: Too big for any one of us. Exactly right for all of us.

codex.title: Cross-border projects
codex.body: Cross-border grids, rail corridors and shared industry hubs achieve scale no single actor can. The EU's connected market decarbonizes faster than any member could alone.

cards.name: Climate Club
cards.flavor: Members trade in the currency of the future.

codex.title: Carbon-standard trade
codex.body: Members trade on a common carbon standard and pool green finance. The club grows because staying outside costs more than joining - the enforcement mechanism the Paris Agreement lacks.

cards.name: Fund a Transition
cards.flavor: Their coal plant, our money, everyone's sky.

codex.title: International climate finance
codex.body: Just Energy Transition Partnerships (South Africa, Indonesia, Vietnam) buy the world's cheapest emission cuts: retiring a coal plant abroad beats a marginal cut at home on every ledger but the political one.

cards.name: Emissions Treaty
cards.flavor: A signature that bends a curve.

codex.title: Binding sectoral treaties
codex.body: Treaties bend national emission curves: the Montreal Protocol remains the most successful environmental agreement ever, eliminating nearly 99% of ozone-depleting substances.

cards.name: Fusion Moonshot
cards.flavor: A star in a bottle, or an invoice in a drawer.

codex.title: Fusion energy
codex.body: Fusion crossed net energy gain at NIF in 2022, but a commercial plant remains decades of engineering away. High ceiling, real odds of arriving too late - the textbook push-your-luck bet.

cards.name: Direct Air Capture
cards.flavor: Vacuum the sky. Terms and conditions apply.

codex.title: Direct air capture
codex.body: Machines that scrub CO2 from ambient air work today at small scale (Climeworks' Orca). Whether costs fall fast enough to matter is an open bet - IPCC pathways lean on it; critics call it a promise to delay.

cards.name: Emergency Relief Corps
cards.flavor: First on the ground, last to leave.

codex.title: Civil protection corps
codex.body: Trained civil-protection corps cut disaster mortality dramatically; Bangladesh reduced cyclone deaths a hundred-fold since 1970 with shelters, warning systems and drilled volunteers.

cards.name: Water Stewardship
cards.flavor: Every drop budgeted like the treasure it is.

codex.title: Water efficiency
codex.body: Watershed restoration, drip irrigation and leak repair stretch every drop. Water efficiency is adaptation and mitigation at once, since moving and treating water burns energy.

cards.name: Coastal Defense Works
cards.flavor: The sea negotiates with no one; the shore must.

codex.title: Living shorelines
codex.body: Restored wetlands and reefs in front of levees outperform concrete alone - and get stronger, not weaker, as they grow.

cards.name: Community Kitchens
cards.flavor: Nobody organizes like people fed together.

codex.title: Community food security
codex.body: Shared kitchens appear wherever disasters strike - and keep working afterward as civic anchors. Food security is the fastest way to hold social trust through a shock.

cards.name: Grid Repair Crews
cards.flavor: Keep the lights on; keep the trust on.

codex.title: Grid resilience
codex.body: Distributed repair capacity and microgrids keep power on through extreme weather. Every blackout avoided is public trust retained for the transition.

cards.name: Mutual Aid Network
cards.flavor: The disaster plan is knowing your neighbors.

codex.title: Mutual aid
codex.body: After every major disaster, most first rescues are made by neighbors, not agencies. Organized mutual aid is measurable resilience - social capital is infrastructure.

cards.name: Heatwave Response Plan
cards.flavor: Cool rooms, checked doors, shifted hours.

codex.title: Heat action plans
codex.body: Cooling centers, buddy checks on the elderly and adjusted work hours cut heatwave mortality at almost no cost. Ahmedabad's 2013 plan became the template for hundreds of cities.
